svg.title: The observation-limited battle controller (v4): what each side may see, what it must imagine, and how it decides
svg.text: Visible to the policy (public state)
own Pokémon: moves, HP, energy, IVs, buffs, cooldowns
opponent species that have appeared and their forms
opponent HP bar, rounded to 1%
shield counts and switch clocks of both sides
moves the opponent has actually used (after they resolve)
energy estimate from counted fast and charged moves
observations.js · perfect counting, no lag or misreads yet
Withheld (known only to the simulator)
unrevealed backline Pokémon and their moves
the opponent’s exact energy, IVs, attack/defence, max HP
the move the opponent is about to throw, or has queued
the charged move awaiting the shield decision
tests change hidden state and check decisions stay identical;
poisoned hidden arguments throw on any access
Beliefs about what is hidden
unknown moves start as the published recommended set;
an observed move replaces its slot
backline: 3 sampled lineups from a 2,048-team bank drawn
from the same opponent meta, filtered to the revealed
species (fallback: weighted marginal draws)
unknown IVs: default initialisation
--belief-samples 3 · the bank is saved in the report for exact replay
Decisions
switch: every 4 turns (or at low HP), compare staying with each
bench member; roll each imagined lineup 24 steps forward,
take the opponent’s worst-case reply, average over lineups;
switch only if it beats staying by ≥ 0.08
attack: cheapest useful charged move while shields remain,
else energy-efficient or lethal · shield: expected damage ≥ 35% HP
lookahead-v4.js · seeded by own state + public view only
Why this controller, and its cost
PvPoke’s Champion AI reads the opponent’s real moves and
energy. A team scored under full information can win on
counter-switches no human could make, so the ranking
would reward the wrong teams. v4 draws the line at what a
player sees on screen.
Terminal value of a rollout (side A − side B):
HP×(1 + 0.18·energy) of living members
+ 0.32 × shields + 0.24 × roster coverage
− 0.12 × switch-lock cost
Costs: more simulation per battle (bounded by headless
mode and branch caches); a 128-fixture parity check
gave 50.8% vs the old controller — realism, not proven
strength. Labels from v1–v3 cannot be reused.
Open: delayed catches, mixed strategies, full-roster
continuation, learned terminal value, realistic counting
errors and lag; several policy styles for stress tests
training/next/OBSERVATION_CONTROLLER.md
Both teams in every simulated battle use this same controller, so neither side has an information advantage.
